MCD.rationale: McDonald's Q1 2026 results showed solid YoY growth (revenue +9%, EPS +7%) with 3.8% global comparable sales growth across all segments, and the franchise model continues to generate exceptional ~45% operating margins. However, several factors temper the view: (1) QoQ trajectory is negative with revenue -7.9% and EPS -12.6% from Q3 2025 levels, reflecting seasonal softness and consumer headwinds; (2) the balance sheet carries negative equity (-$1.29B) reflecting heavy leverage and capital returns; (3) operating cash flow declined QoQ to $2.41B from $3.43B; (4) the stock has already corrected -12.3% over the past quarter to $283.70, sitting near its 52-week low of $282.15, which provides some valuation cushion but the P/E data is unavailable to confirm cheapness vs history; (5) macro headwinds are real — oil at ~$98/barrel (+52% over the period) pressures consumer spending and drive-thru traffic, with management noting consumer spending 'getting a little bit worse'; (6) the Q1 earnings beat (adjusted EPS $2.83 vs $2.75 consensus) is a modest positive catalyst but guidance for weaker Q2 sales due to tough comps limits the re-rating potential. The business quality is undeniable — 95% franchised, ~210M loyalty users, 49-year dividend growth streak — but near-term trajectory is mixed and the stock is not clearly cheap enough to warrant a stronger score.
